title: How Many Bishops To BEAT Magnus?
summary: 'How many bishops to beat the Magnus bot': the creator has only his king plus N bishops (no pawns) against chess.com's Magnus bot (2882) with a full army, starting with 2 bishops and adding one after each loss. The bot keeps trapping/skewering bishops and closing the centre. It took 14 bishops to finally checkmate Magnus (a careful K+B mate at the end while avoiding stalemate). Also plugs his first livestream (Jan 12, 10pm ET).
rules: Player (White): king + N bishops only; Magnus bot (Black): full standard army.
Start N=2; after each loss add one bishop (placed alternating light/dark squares along the first ranks).
Normal chess rules; stalemate is a draw (he avoids it in the final mate).
